data.title: Mailbox Contents Accessible After Token Theft
data.summary:
A stolen session token granted full access to mailbox contents without re-authentication,
and the access was not distinguished from legitimate use by any conditional access or
alerting rule.
data.description:
Token theft bypasses multi-factor authentication entirely: the token is issued after
authentication has already succeeded, so replaying it requires no credential and no second
factor.

Mail is the highest-value target available, because it contains the material for onward
fraud, the history of every relationship, and frequently the password reset path for other
systems. Automated forwarding and mailbox rules extend the access beyond the lifetime of
the token, and are commonly overlooked in remediation.

Detection depends on noticing that an established session is being used from a different
location, device or client than it was issued to — which requires continuous evaluation
rather than a check at sign-in only.
data.recommendation:
* Enable token protection and continuous access evaluation so a session is re-evaluated
  rather than trusted until expiry.
* Apply conditional access requiring compliant devices for mail access.
* Alert on new mailbox forwarding rules and on mass download from a mailbox.
* Include token revocation in incident response, since a password reset alone does not
  invalidate an existing session.
data.short_recommendation: Enable continuous access evaluation and revoke tokens during response.
